raw_response:
I'm 58 years old and I've been farming my 7 mu of land in Quzhou County for over 35 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and I listen to what the extension agent says at the village meetings, but at the end of the day I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some paper tells me. It's March now and my winter wheat is greening up — I planted it last October using an improved variety, Jimai 32, bought from the county supply store. The stand looks decent this year, not the best I've had but better than the drought year. I'm sticking with the wheat-maize double crop system. That's what this land is made for and at my age I don't have the back for picking cotton like my cousin in the western village. My son works in Handan now so it's mostly me out here, with some hired help at harvest when the window is tight.

For the wheat already in the ground, the extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is the science-based rate, but last year I did 15 and the wheat looked a bit yellow at jointing, so this year I'm going with 18 kg N per mu — better to waste a few yuan than lose half a harvest. I'll add about 6 kg of phosphorus and 4 kg of potassium too, split between spring topdressing and what I put down last autumn. I'll irrigate three times: once at green-up in March, once at jointing in April, and once at grain filling in May. The pumping costs hurt, but dry wheat is worthless. I'll spray twice — once for weeds and once for aphids when they show up in May. No tillage needed now since the crop is already growing.

After I harvest the wheat in early June — probably around June 8th if the weather holds — I'll immediately plant hybrid maize, Zhengdan 958. That's the only way to go for corn. The turnaround is brutal, maybe five or six days, so I'll hire my neighbor Li's rotary tiller to prep the seedbed right behind the combine. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at jointing, totaling about 16 kg N, 5 kg P, and 4 kg K per mu. Maize doesn't need as much babying as wheat — two irrigations should do it, at jointing and filling, unless the summer is bone dry like 2022. Two pesticide sprays: one pre-emergence herbicide and one insecticide when the borers come in July.

I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat and 550 kg per mu from the maize if the weather is normal. Last year I got 480 and 520, so I'm hoping for a little better but not counting on it. I don't grow vegetables or anything else — grain is easy to sell, the county station buys wheat, and the corn dealer drives his truck to the village edge. At 58, I'm not chasing new crops or fancy schemes. I know this system, it feeds my family, and it pays the bills.
